subtitle: A microphone turns listening into a game

body: SingStar is London Studio's PlayStation 2 karaoke game, introduced in Europe in May 2004. Players sing along to familiar recordings using USB microphones while the game measures their performance. Lyrics and pitch guidance make the song visible, allowing the television to become the centre of a shared singing session. The red and blue microphones give two people an immediate role in front of the screen. The idea depends less on learning an unusual controller than on choosing a song somebody already knows and giving them a reason to sing it aloud.

The display connects the words to a guide for the notes, giving feedback while the recording continues. Scoring turns a familiar song into a challenge that can be repeated or shared with another singer. The microphone makes performance visible in a different way from pressing a button: the player's own voice becomes the input. A gathering can move from watching someone else to taking part as soon as a microphone changes hands. That simple transition helped the game fit into social occasions where people had very different levels of experience with games.

Later editions expanded the available music and produced regional releases for different audiences. Camera support also allowed singers to see and record themselves, connecting the performance to the room around the console. The series continued on PlayStation 3 and PlayStation 4, where online song purchases enlarged its library. Those services closed in January 2020 while existing offline content remained accessible. The original PlayStation 2 game established the essential arrangement: a recording, a readable guide and two microphones that invited the people beside the television to become the entertainment.
